messages:
sre-oncall: apiserver pods in us-west1 started OOMKilling ~20m ago. controlplane latency + watch queue errors. controller-manager also logs lease renew failures. anyone on-call seeing this? :warning:
ops-bot: [ALERT] k8s/apiserver OOMKill rate > 5/min in cluster-us-west1 (alert 1964001122).
maya: I see it — 3/5 apiserver replicas restarted in the last 15m. heap looks big in the last metrics spike. grabbing logs now.
leo: can you paste the apiserver pod logs? suspect watch cache growth or a large informer storm from a deployment.
sre-oncall: logs snippet:
```
I0321 10:12:33.123456 1 cacher.go:215] watch cache size: objects=1,354,212
E0321 10:12:34.654321 1 server.go:286] runtime: out of memory: cannot allocate 524288 bytes
panic: runtime: out of memory
```
maya: yep huge watch cache count. Did we recently roll a job that re-created lots of small pods?
sam: we had a mass rollout in staging, not prod. but last deploy in prod touched a controller that lists pods. check controller-manager churn.
nina: controller-manager logs show frequent informer reconnects and increasing goroutine count. maybe a leak after a failing rollout hook.
leo: immediate mitigation: reduce apiserver memory limit/requests? that won't help. Better: 1) scale apiserver replicas temporarily to 7, 2) kick controller-manager (restart) to drop stuck watch clients, 3) enable prefix compaction for watch cache?
sre-oncall: taking actions: cordoning node k8s-usw1-control-3 where OOMs land, scaling apiserver to 7 in control plane pool.
ops-bot: runbook action logged: scale deployment kube-apiserver -> 7 replicas (cmd: kubectl -n kube-system scale deploy/kube-apiserver --replicas=7).
maya: restarted controller-manager on us-west1-ctrlplane-2, monitoring.
leo: while doing that, we should also check etcd memory/backpressure. if apiserver keeps rebuilding caches it will hammer etcd.
sam: etcd shows occasional leader latency spikes but not sustained. disk i/o fine.
nina: hypothesis: a client (third-party or automated job) started listing huge numbers of resources; apiserver's watch cache ballooned. we should add a temporary rate limit on unauth requests and inspect audit logs for heavy list calls.
sre-oncall: audit logs show a bot user 'infra-sync' doing repeated LIST requests to /api/v1/pods from 10.9.32.110. throttling it now via network policy and limiting its token.
leo: good. after restarting controller-manager and throttling infra-sync, watch cache dropped from 1.3M -> 42k over 6 minutes.
maya: apiserver OOMs stopped. latency back to normal. keeping controlplane at 7 replicas for next 2 hours and will implement a safer memory limit for apiserver and add alert for watch cache size.
sre-oncall: follow-ups: 1) root-cause ticket to infra-sync owners for runaway LIST loops, 2) add watch-cache-size alert + deploy compacting config, 3) consider circuit-breaker on controller-manager restarts. documenting in postmortem. :thumbsup:
ops-bot: incident resolved (1964002378): apiserver OOMs ceased, controlplane latency normalized.
